description: Invented Acme Outdoor Gear blog posts. Labels: must_mention (terms every social post should carry), risky_source (the post contains a claim that should not be repeated in social copy) and the risky phrases themselves. Items marked heldout were never used while tuning prompts or rules.

input.title: Packing list for the Tongariro Alpine Crossing
input.body: The Tongariro Alpine Crossing is 19.4 km and most people take 6 to 8 hours. Weather on the saddle changes fast, so pack a rain shell, a warm layer, a hat and gloves even in summer. Carry at least 2 litres of water per person; there is none on the track. Our Trailhead 45L pack has room for all of it plus lunch. Start early, check the forecast the night before, and book a shuttle in advance.

input.title: Meet the Kea 3-season tent
input.body: The Kea is our new two-person, 3-season tent. It weighs 1.9 kg, pitches in about five minutes and has two doors so nobody climbs over anyone at 2 am. The fly is rated to 3,000 mm. It's available from 1 November for $449 in stores and online. It's not built for snow camping; for that, look at the Alpine 4-season range.

input.title: Why our Fiordland jacket is the best rain jacket in New Zealand
input.body: The Fiordland jacket is 100% waterproof and guaranteed to keep you dry in any storm. It uses a 3-layer membrane rated to 20,000 mm, fully taped seams and pit zips for venting. It weighs 380 g and packs into its own pocket. Price: $329. Customers have worn it on the Milford Track in serious rain.

input.title: Spring sale: 20% off sleeping bags
input.body: From 10 to 20 October, all Alpine sleeping bags are 20% off in stores and online. That includes the Alpine 0 (rated to 0 degrees comfort) and the Alpine -5. Stock is limited in the long sizes. The sale doesn't apply to wholesale orders or gift cards.

input.title: How to dry out a wet tent
input.body: Packing a wet tent is sometimes unavoidable. When you get home, pitch it or hang it within 24 hours so mould doesn't start. Open both doors, wipe out sand and grit, and let it dry out of direct sun if you can, since UV breaks down the fabric over time. Never put a tent in the dryer. Store it loosely in a cool, dry cupboard rather than tightly rolled.

input.title: Our new Wellington store opens on 14 November
input.body: We're opening our fourth store at 22 Cuba Street, Wellington on Saturday 14 November. Come along from 9 am for free coffee, a gear-repair demo at 11 am, and a talk from a local search-and-rescue volunteer at 2 pm. The first 50 customers get a free Acme drink bottle.

input.title: The Ember 2 stove: clinically proven to cook faster
input.body: The Ember 2 is clinically proven to boil water faster than any other stove on the market. It boils a litre in about 3.5 minutes in our own tests, weighs 85 g and folds into a 6 cm case. It runs on standard screw-on gas canisters. Always cook outside your tent: stoves produce carbon monoxide. Price $89.

input.title: Five day walks near Christchurch
input.body: Christchurch has great walking right on its doorstep. Our five favourites: the Bridle Path (about 2 hours return), Godley Head loop (3 hours), Mount Herbert from Diamond Harbour (5 to 6 hours), Rapaki Track (1.5 hours) and the Avon River walk (flat, as long as you like). Take water and a layer; the Port Hills get windy.

input.title: Our gear repair service is now free for life
input.body: Every Acme jacket, pack and tent can now be repaired at any of our stores. Simple fixes like zips, buckles and seam tape are free for the first two years; after that we charge cost price. Most repairs take 7 to 10 days. Bring the item clean and dry, and we'll give you a quote before we start.

input.title: Layering 101 for winter tramping
input.body: Three layers keep you comfortable in winter: a merino or synthetic base layer that moves sweat away, a fleece or puffer mid layer for warmth, and a waterproof shell to stop wind and rain. Avoid cotton, which stays wet. Our Merino 200 base layer is $119 and the Ridge fleece is $139. Adjust layers before you get sweaty, not after.

input.title: Introducing the Trailhead 55L pack
input.body: The Trailhead 55L is built for multi-day tramps. It has an adjustable back length for torsos 40 to 52 cm, a removable lid that becomes a day pack, and hip-belt pockets big enough for a phone. It weighs 1.6 kg. Available now for $299 in three colours.

input.title: Kids' rain ponchos that never leak
input.body: Our new kids' rain ponchos never leak and are completely safe for children of all ages. They come in sizes 4 to 12, fold into a small pouch, and have reflective strips on the back. $39 each, or $35 each for school orders of 20 or more.

input.title: Black Friday: 30% off packs, one day only
input.body: On Friday 27 November, every pack in our range is 30% off, online and in all four stores. The sale runs from midnight to midnight NZ time. Click and collect orders must be picked up by 6 December. Not available on wholesale orders.

input.title: Leave No Trace: seven simple habits
input.body: Leave No Trace comes down to seven habits: plan ahead, stay on durable surfaces, pack out all rubbish, leave what you find, keep fires small or use a stove, respect wildlife, and be considerate of other visitors. Carry a small rubbish bag in your pack; it weighs nothing and makes a big difference.

input.title: The Lumen headlamp: brightest headlamp ever made
input.body: The Lumen is the brightest headlamp ever made, with 400 lumens on high and up to 40 hours on low. It charges by USB-C in 3 hours and weighs 72 g with the battery. It's rated IPX4, so it handles rain but not swimming. Price $79.
